title: Least Squares Solution to Overdetermined Systems

statement.text: Find the least squares solution to the inconsistent system $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ where $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{b} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}$.

reflectionPrompt.question: Why might this system have no exact solution?
reflectionPrompt.hint: 3 equations but only 2 unknowns - the system is overdetermined and generally inconsistent.

options.content: Overdetermined system (more equations than unknowns) - generally has no exact solution

correct.explanation: Correct! With 3 equations and 2 unknowns, $\mathbf{b}$ is unlikely to lie in the column space of $A$. We seek the "best" approximate solution.

incorrect.b: Underdetermined means fewer equations than unknowns. Here we have MORE equations (3) than unknowns (2).
incorrect.c: Overdetermined systems generally have no solution - need least squares approximation!

currentState.description: This transforms overdetermined system to square system.

correct.insight: $A^TA$ is always square and symmetric. If $A$ has full column rank, $A^TA$ is invertible.

incorrect.b: Need to compute the matrix products! $A^TA$ is $2 \times 2$ with entries from inner products of columns.
incorrect.c: $A^TA$ is generally not diagonal. Compute the off-diagonal entries!

reflectionPrompt.question: What is the least squares solution $\hat{\mathbf{x}}$?

correct.explanation: Excellent! Solving the normal equations: $3x_1 + 6x_2 = 5$ and $6x_1 + 14x_2 = 11$ gives $x_1 = 1/3$, $x_2 = 2/3$.

incorrect.b: Check: $A\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} \neq \mathbf{b}$. Not the solution to normal equations!
incorrect.c: Solve the system carefully. Use elimination or substitution.

options.content: $A\hat{\mathbf{x}} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 5/3 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} \approx \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1.67 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}$ (best approximation to $\mathbf{b}$ in column space of $A$)

correct.explanation: Correct! $A\hat{\mathbf{x}} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 5/3 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}$ is the closest point to $\mathbf{b}$ in $\text{col}(A)$. Residual: $\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{b} - A\hat{\mathbf{x}} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1/3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}$.
correct.insight: Least squares gives the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{b}$ onto the column space of $A$!

incorrect.b: System is inconsistent - no exact solution exists. This is the BEST approximation.
incorrect.c: Least squares ALWAYS gives a best approximation (when $A$ has full column rank).

keyInsights: Overdetermined system: 3 equations, 2 unknowns - generally inconsistent
Normal equations: $A^TA\mathbf{x} = A^T\mathbf{b}$ (always consistent when $A$ has full column rank)
summary.fullSolution:
**Least squares solution to $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$**

**Given:** $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$, $\mathbf{b} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}$

**Normal equations:** $A^TA\mathbf{x} = A^T\mathbf{b}$

**Compute $A^TA$:**
$$A^TA = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 6 \\ 6 & 14 \end{bmatrix}$$

**Compute $A^T\mathbf{b}$:**
$$A^T\mathbf{b} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 11 \end{bmatrix}$$

**Solve:**
$$\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 6 \\ 6 & 14 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 11 \end{bmatrix}$$

From row 1: $3x_1 + 6x_2 = 5$
From row 2: $6x_1 + 14x_2 = 11$

Solving: $x_1 = \frac{1}{3}$, $x_2 = \frac{2}{3}$

**Least squares solution:** $\hat{\mathbf{x}} = \begin{bmatrix} 1/3 \\ 2/3 \end{bmatrix}$
